claims.claim: The Dramatica Co. asserts that asking a model for ambiguity returns ambiguity as surface texture rather than as a structural consequence of the story.
claims.quote: ambiguity as a texture rather than as a structural consequence

claims.claim: The Dramatica Co. asserts that prompting away AI punctuation leaves the model's narrative habits intact.
claims.quote: prompt away the punctuation and still leave the machine’s narrative habits intact

claims.claim: Mohammad Siam, replying on X to Ethan Mollick's StoryScope post, wrote that AI explains where humans imply.
claims.source: Mohammad Siam, X reply, 27 May 2026, relayed verbatim by the Dramatica Blog
claims.page: pull-quote in 'AI Likes the Clean Line'

claims.claim: Ethan Mollick, posting on X about the StoryScope preprint, used the phrase 'AI narrative tells' for the layer beneath stylistic tells.
claims.source: Ethan Mollick, X, 27 May 2026, relayed as a pull-quote by the Dramatica Blog
claims.page: pull-quote after the 'Paper Finds Structure, Not Just Style' lead-in

claims.feature: other: what a human editor sees first
claims.claim: Alex Mahadevan, director of Poynter's MediaWise, told the Reuters Institute that most editors shown AI-generated text shake their heads because it is empty.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: they will shake their heads, because it is empty

claims.claim: Mahadevan told the Reuters Institute his dead giveaway for AI writing is a lot of words that do not say anything.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: it's a lot of words that don't say anything

claims.claim: Mahadevan named ChatGPT's tendency to make broad, sweeping, emotional statements as the feature of AI writing he finds most jarring in journalism.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025

claims.claim: Mahadevan predicted that heavy reliance on AI writing would make every news homepage blur into the same voice.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: every homepage blurs into the same voice

claims.claim: Mahadevan asserted the AI default style smooths out dialects, activist language and the ways specific communities actually talk.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: smooth out dialects, activist language and ways specific communities actually talk

claims.feature: other: surface polish with nothing underneath
claims.claim: Dr Tom S. Juzek of Florida State University told the Reuters Institute that ChatGPT broke the link readers used to make between quality of form and quality of content.
claims.source: Tom S. Juzek (Florida State University) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: quality of form and quality of content, and ChatGPT broke that

claims.claim: Juzek and Ward re-ran reinforcement learning from human feedback with their own recruited testers and found that those testers preferred outputs containing AI buzzwords.
claims.source: Marina Adami reporting Juzek and Ward's experiment, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: their testers did prefer outputs that contained AI buzzwords

claims.claim: In Juzek and Ward's RLHF replication the participants who otherwise favoured AI buzzwords tended not to prefer texts containing 'delve' and 'nuanced'.
claims.source: Marina Adami reporting Juzek and Ward's experiment, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: tended not to prefer texts containing ‘delve’ and ‘nuanced’

claims.claim: Mahadevan said he is concerned that readers fixate on quick heuristics to identify AI writing.
claims.source: Alex Mahadevan (Poynter/MediaWise) quoted by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
claims.quote: I do get concerned that we fixate on these quick heuristics

claims.claim: The Reuters Institute reports that so far there is not much evidence that homogenisation of language is happening.
claims.quote: there’s not much evidence that homogenisation is happening

claims.claim: Dr Karolina Rudnicka of the University of Gdansk told the Reuters Institute that ChatGPT and Grammarly avoid slang, contractions, colloquial language and the passive voice when reviewing drafts.
claims.source: Karolina Rudnicka (University of Gdansk) reported by Marina Adami, Reuters Institute, 2025
